content.text:
This confirms the root cause. The pre-existing logic (added in `42809e6`) checked `fieldNameForRoutingKey.startsWith("metadata.")` at `store()` time to decide whether the routing key should be nested under `metadata` or placed at the top level of the document. Commit `c48a5bd` added an unconditional `replaceAll("\\.", "%2E")` on `fieldNameForRoutingKey` during `prepare()`, before that check ever runs. Since the replacement targets *all* periods, a configured value like `metadata.foo` becomes `metadata%2Efoo` — so the later `.startsWith("metadata.")` test always evaluates to `false`, and the field is written to the wrong location (top-level instead of nested under `metadata`, or vice versa for the negated check).

The fix commit (`fea5693`) confirms this diagnosis exactly: it introduces a `routingFieldNameInMetadata` boolean computed and stripped *before* the `%2E` substitution, replacing the now-broken `startsWith("metadata.")` checks — precisely undoing the ordering problem that `c48a5bd` introduced.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: c48a5bd47fe4f38846fae5dd9b6393e3574fd5e7

## Reasoning
(1) I inspected the full history of `StatusUpdaterBolt.java` with `git log --follow -p` and read every change made to the routing-key/`fieldNameForRoutingKey` logic, since the fix commit touches exactly this area.

(2) The bug was introduced in `c48a5bd` ("Normalise fieldNameForRoutingKey; fixes #393"), which added an unconditional `fieldNameForRoutingKey.replaceAll("\\.", "%2E")` in `prepare()`. This runs on the raw config value, including any `metadata.` prefix, turning e.g. `metadata.foo` into `metadata%2Efoo`. The `store()` method (added earlier in `42809e6`) relies on `fieldNameForRoutingKey.startsWith("metadata.")` to decide whether to nest the routing field under `metadata` or place it top-level — a check that silently breaks once the prefix's periods have been escaped.

(3) The fix commit `fea5693` is direct evidence: it adds a `routingFieldNameInMetadata` boolean, computed by checking `startsWith("metadata.")` and stripping the prefix *before* the `%2E` substitution runs, then uses that boolean everywhere instead of the now-unreliable `startsWith`/`substring(9)` calls on the transformed string. This is exactly the ordering bug that `c48a5bd` created by inserting the blanket period-replacement ahead of the prefix-sensitive logic. I'm confident in this attribution — the causal chain (prefix check pre-dates the replaceAll; replaceAll commit breaks it; fix commit reorders/refactors around it) is unambiguous in the commit history.
